official.description_text:
Postdoc in sustainable generative artificial intelligence for media
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The five-year research project FrugalAI is exploring the impacts of using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for the creation of media content. Current genAI models, used for generating music, images, text, and other media, rely on vast data sets and require significant computational resources. Training genAI models and employing them on a global scale contributes to substantial energy consumption, resource depletion, and increased carbon emissions, exacerbating environmental harm. Our project aims to develop and promote an innovative, sustainable alternative to existing large and commercial genAI systems. It aims to reduce the environmental footprint of genAI technologies while fostering positive social impacts by prioritizing small, ethically sourced data sets, local models and compute, and encouraging sustainable behavior among users.
The research and development conducted in the project can be regarded as situated within the area of human-centered AI. FrugalAI has the following objectives:
Estimate the environmental impact of current big-data genAI.
Construct a set of open-source frugal genAI tools based on small, ethical data.
Map the impact on social sustainability that emerges from using frugal genAI.
Compare the environmental impact of these tools with big-data genAI tools.
Propose and apply evaluation metrics that consider resource use.
Investigate implications for other genAI applications (e.g., image generation).
The postdoctoral researcher, having a background related to HCI and machine learning, will contribute to all objectives over a period of two years at 100% time. Working with a diverse team of engineers, musicologists, and designers, the job will include the following tasks:
Contribute to the development of an interactive online broadcasting environment (a prototype is “Stochastic Pirate Radio” KSPR) by designing and maintaining project software, and developing pipelines for creating media programs and the automated monitoring for offensive content, and estimating and tracking energy usage.
Research and develop frugal AI principles to reduce model sizes, data, and computation using the state of the art in machine learning.
Develop a multi-objective metric of genAI sustainability (environmental, economic, sociocultural), building from C. Douwes,
On the Environmental Impact of Deep Generative Models for Audio
, Doctoral dissertation, Sorbonne Université 2023).
Help organize and run workshops with team members
For more information, contact Bob L. T. Sturm (
bobs@kth.se
).

Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality

ai.summary: KTH postdoc (2 years, Stockholm) developing sustainable generative AI for media production, combining HCI and machine learning to reduce environmental impact of GenAI systems through frugal principles, smaller models, and ethical datasets. The role emphasizes interactive system design, sustainability metrics, and collaborative workshop facilitation alongside technical ML work.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is fundamentally about generative AI algorithm development and sustainability metrics for media GenAI—pure machine learning territory. While it mentions 'human-centered AI' as a framing concept, the actual work (frugal model compression, energy tracking pipelines, multi-objective sustainability metrics) sits in ML systems and environmental impact assessment, not human-centered design or interaction. The researcher's expertise in spatial cognition, wayfinding, collaborative immersive systems, and educational XR has no thematic alignment with audio/media GenAI sustainability.

methodological_fit.rationale: The position requires 'HCI and machine learning' background, which superficially matches the researcher's profile. However, methodological fit is weak. The researcher has strong HCI experimental design (user studies, quantitative spatial measures, wayfinding metrics) but the posted tasks demand ML algorithm development (model compression, frugal principles), software engineering (pipeline design, monitoring systems), and sustainability science—not human-centered evaluation. The workshop facilitation is a minor element. The researcher's quantitative methods (questionnaires, task performance) are HCI-oriented; the role needs ML engineering and systems thinking.

growth_value.rationale: Limited closure of strategic gaps. The researcher would gain exposure to generative AI systems and sustainability assessment, which broaden HCI perspective. However, this position would push the researcher toward pure ML and systems optimization—directly contrary to their stated target identity (human-centered XR/HCI researcher, not ML engineer). The role offers no development in immersive systems, spatial cognition, collaborative interaction design, or learning science. Growth would be orthogonal to PhD trajectory.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong technical institution with international visibility; Stockholm is in a preferred region. However, strategic value is undermined by fundamental misalignment. The researcher's target PhD pathway emphasizes human-centered immersive systems and collaborative spatial learning (Aalto, TU Delft, European HCI groups). A postdoc in sustainable GenAI signals a pivot toward AI systems and sustainability research—a different research identity than the stated target. Supervisor (Bob Sturm, audio/music ML specialist) and project (FrugalAI) are not positioned in HCI or XR communities. This would require narrative reframing at PhD application.

eligibility_flags: Requires doctoral degree (PhD) or equivalent by start date; researcher holds only MSc by Research (in progress thesis stage). Doctoral requirement is a hard eligibility barrier unless thesis completion and graduation occur before employment decision.
Posting mentions potential security clearance under Swedish Protective Security Act; researcher should verify EU/non-EU status implications.

Role emphasizes 'HCI and machine learning' background; researcher has strong HCI but beginner-level Python and no demonstrated ML systems or algorithm development experience. Fit to stated ML requirement is questionable.
risks: Career trajectory risk: accepting a postdoc in sustainable GenAI before PhD would establish researcher identity in ML/sustainability rather than human-centered XR, complicating future positioning in target HCI/XR communities.

Skill gap: position tasks (frugal model compression, energy tracking pipelines, sustainability metrics) require applied ML systems expertise the researcher has not demonstrated. Ramp-up would be steep.

Methodological mismatch: researcher's strength is human-centered experimental design for spatial cognition; this role prioritizes ML algorithm development and technical systems engineering. Day-to-day work would be outside core expertise.
Supervisor alignment: Bob Sturm's group focuses on audio/music and generative models; no stated connection to HCI, immersive systems, or learning science. Limited mentorship for target PhD identity.

PhD preparation: a 2-year postdoc in GenAI sustainability would delay entry to PhD programs in human-centered XR and potentially weaken candidacy for Aalto/TU Delft HCI groups seeking researchers with focused immersive-systems expertise.
